paper.title: What Memory Do GUI Agents Really Need? From Passive Records to Active Task-Driving States
paper.central_claim: GUI-agent memory should be an agent-maintained, structured, item-status-tracking execution state (ATMem) rather than a passive record; trained by verified SFT and interventional memory-ON/OFF online RL (STR-GRPO), ATMem-UI reaches 76.6% on AndroidWorld with 8B, 23.3% on unseen-environment MobileWorld, and does best among end-to-end agents on the new DataScope benchmark.
paper.claim_type_aggregate_reason: The central claim is closed-loop online success of an agent whose observe-act loop is changed (an agent-maintained execution state injected every step), plus the training recipe that makes it used; the headline numbers are end-to-end AndroidWorld/MobileWorld success. son55's reading adopted; it changes interpretation only.

preliminary_evidence_judgment: Read before seat scores (HTML plus authoritative PDF supplement Boxes A.3/A.7). ATMem is an agent-written JSON execution state (phase, context, schema fields, items with remaining/finished/skipped) carried in the system prompt; SFT on 21.7K verifier-gated GPT-5+UIIns steps from 120 own templates on a 20-app virtual Android platform, then STR-GRPO with balanced memory-ON/OFF rollouts and a memory-activity penalty. AndroidWorld 76.6 (8B) is in-domain: the training platform and DataScope use AndroidWorld apps (Markor, Broccoli, Simple SMS ...), no overlap analysis. MobileWorld (declared unseen) 23.3 is claimed to beat the strongest baseline by 36.2% relative, but the pinned MAI-UI report (the same GUI-only column from which ATMem's other MobileWorld rows are copied: UI-Venus-72B 16.4, GUI-Owl-7B 7.7, Qwen3-VL-8B 9.4) lists MAI-UI-8B 27.5 and Doubao-1.5-UI-TARS 26.3; both are baselines elsewhere in this paper yet omitted from Table 2. Ablation chain lacks an ATMem-free SFT arm; flat-memory comparison is a single case.

signatures.object: Agent-written structured execution state (ATMem) carried in the system prompt: workflow fields (phase, remaining/completed files, constraints) and schema-level item entries with status.
signatures.information: Instruction, current screenshot, history, previous memory block; the agent updates memory each turn; teacher (LLM planner + UIIns) generates SFT memory states.
signatures.operation: SFT on 21,713 verifier-gated steps from 1.1K executable instances, then online RL.
signatures.output: Memory block, reasoning trace, executable GUI action per step.
signatures.conditions: Data-dependent multi-item cross-app workflows; memory empty when not needed.
signatures.feedback: Terminal-state verifier V in {0,1} and a memory-active cost.
signatures.selection_rule: SFT: keep trajectories whose terminal state passes the verifier. RL: group-normalised advantage over a balanced ON/OFF mixture.
signatures.persistence: Memory persists within the episode only; training result persists in policy weights.
signatures.later_use: Next-step prompt; evaluation on AndroidWorld, MobileWorld, DataScope.
signatures.failure_boundary: Stuck loops, wrong termination and step caps remain; DataScope SR stays at 1-2 of 32.

signatures.information: Same task, same initial state; half the rollouts mask the memory channel.
signatures.operation: Reward R = V(terminal) - alpha*z*rho (fraction of memory-active steps); advantage over the pooled group; ATMem tokens masked from loss in OFF rollouts.
signatures.conditions: Memory-OFF rollouts see a state the SFT policy was not trained on (OFF is out-of-distribution for imitation).
signatures.failure_boundary: alpha not reported; effect measured in single runs.

signatures.object: DataScope benchmark: 32 templates x 3 difficulty levels, target and same-schema distractor counts scaled.
signatures.information: Initializer writes targets/distractors into app storage; verifiers read terminal app state; metrics SR, App-Prog, Scope-F1.
signatures.operation: Template instantiation by LLM, verifier synthesis, calibration against controlled terminal-state variants.
signatures.selection_rule: verifier retained only if all calibration cases match
signatures.claimed_effect: Exposes stuck loops (40.9% of MAI-UI failures).

gap.author_gap: Passive records of past observations do not give stable execution-state awareness for long-horizon, multi-item, cross-app GUI workflows, causing missed, repeated or over-scoped operations.
gap.checked_gap: Supported by failure analysis of a baseline (stuck loops 40.9%) and an illustrative flat-note failure, and by the 83% data-operation share in AndroidWorld; but the quantitative flat-memory comparison sits in a figure, and the DataScope benchmark is built by the same authors around the claimed bottleneck.
lineage: Mobile-Agent-E / v2 notes memory, AgentProg program-based context, UI-Mem, MemGUI-Bench, AndroTMem and others (cited in Related Work, not pinned)
MAI-UI online RL infrastructure (pinned; their stated basis for the RL stack)
AWM/SkillWeaver-type cross-episode memory (pinned) are experience-oriented, a different axis
gap.lineage_note: Related Work separates experience-oriented from execution-oriented memory; closest execution-oriented neighbours are not available locally. MAI-UI (pinned) gives the 8B baseline at 70.7 and a 235B model at 76.7.
gap.closest_adjacent: Recording-centric note memory (Mobile-Agent-E) compared qualitatively; AgentProg for belief-state tracking.
gap.residue: Wrong termination and step-cap failures; DataScope floor effects.
gap.method_response: Make the memory itself a structured per-item status board and train when to use it.
gap.remaining_gap: Isolating the structure effect from in-environment SFT; quantitative comparison with other execution-oriented memories.
unresolved: Is the +23.1 SFT gain due to ATMem or in-environment data?
gap.aggregate_neighbor_check: Pinned MAI-UI report used for the comparison check: ATMem's MobileWorld table omits two stronger baselines from the same source column; pinned AndroidWorld confirms app overlap with the training/DataScope apps.

condition_checks.condition_definition: Synthesised tasks are filtered to a difficulty band before RL training (2510.17790#s2).

condition_checks.reason: Constructed success/failure calibration; no independent legal/faulty pools with error rates.
condition_checks.condition_definition: Checkers/oracles are assessed on independent pools of faulty and legal implementations, measuring false rejects of legal alternatives as well as detection of failures (2610.05001#s2).

condition_checks.reason: Residual checker error not quantified beyond constructed tests.
condition_checks.condition_definition: Residual false positives/negatives are not quantified, and checkpoint weights are LLM-chosen and unvalidated (2404.07972#s1, 2601.04126#s2); two-sided validation remains a survey recommendation, not measured; must_include and GPT-4 fuzzy match can accept partially wrong content (2610.05001#s2, 2610.05001#s3, 2307.13854#s3, 2401.13649#s3).

condition_checks.reason: Generation plus manual repair reduces labor but no measured annotation hours.
condition_checks.condition_definition: Checkers are per-task manual work (~2 man-hours each) and do not exist for unannotated tasks (2404.07972#s1).

condition_checks.reason: Real apps, but restricted inspectable app states.
condition_checks.condition_name: Synthetic environments without real server logic
condition_checks.condition_definition: Generated sites have no real server logic and are single-site, single-user in scope; benchmark apps are restricted to ones without login and with inspectable local storage, or clones with sampled data (2601.04126#s1, 2405.14573#s1, 2307.13854#s1).

condition_checks.reason: Train/spec overlap beyond MW assertion not enumerated.
condition_checks.condition_definition: Overlap between synthesised tasks and the test distribution is not analysed (2510.17790#s2).

condition_checks.reason: Incremental STR SR gains1.8/2.6 need variance; not zero benefit.
condition_checks.condition_definition: Evaluator-first tasks are harder and fewer, and the RL gain is ~2 points (2510.17790#s2).

condition_checks.reason: State checker plus GUI observations, not screen-only truth.
condition_checks.condition_definition: Screenshots alone cannot see some state (e.g. file size), so screenshot judges and scripts are complementary; a design relying on one alone misses cases (2404.07972#s1).

matches.reason: K12 is actual reward/evaluation operation. K34 is only partial comparator: calibration is stronger than no audit but not independent two-sided implementation pools.

condition_checks.reason: Verifier-gated SFT precedes onlineRL.
condition_checks.condition_definition: Online RL starts from an SFT/offline-trained policy; ~1k online trajectories suffice on short AitW tasks (2406.11896#s1, 2411.02337#s3).

condition_checks.reason: Clipped on-policy update; no demonstrated replay/perplexity-band recipe.
condition_checks.condition_definition: Updates are KL-constrained to the previous-phase policy and replay successful trajectories within a perplexity band; tasks are curriculum-filtered for informativeness (2411.02337#s3, 2406.11896#s1).

condition_checks.reason: No first-error correction data contribution.
condition_checks.condition_definition: Training data corrects the first erroneous step and adds a recovery action after it; reflection data raises level-2 success 14.58% -> 23.61%, online reflection tuning 23.61% -> 34.72%, and DPO on corrected vs erroneous actions improves OSWorld (72B 18.8 -> 22.7) (2506.08012#s1, 2506.08012#s2, 2501.12326#s1).

condition_checks.reason: Terminal-accepted trajectories, not action-matching thought filtering.
condition_checks.condition_definition: Generated per-step thoughts are kept only when the sampled action matches ground truth (bootstrapping), avoiding superficial rationalisation (2501.12326#s2, 2412.04454#s2).

condition_checks.reason: Training/evaluation are executable, not semi-online proxy.
condition_checks.condition_name: Offline proxy validated against online success
condition_checks.condition_definition: A semi-online/offline protocol is shown to correlate with online success (SOP vs AndroidWorld, R^2=0.934) (2509.11543#s3).

condition_checks.reason: No mixed reasoning-level contribution.
condition_checks.condition_name: Mixed reasoning levels with the decoding level ablated
condition_checks.condition_definition: Reasoning annotations synthesised by a strong MLLM are trained as a mixture of levels and the level used at decoding is ablated (mixing L1/L2/L3 and decoding L2: OSWorld 18.5% vs 13.1% L2-only; reflective long CoT 11.5% -> 15.3%) (2508.09123#s2, 2508.09123#s3, 2312.08914#s3).

condition_checks.reason: Long-phase stability and replay need not be inferred from clipped updates.
condition_checks.condition_definition: Without KL or replay, performance degrades over phases; replaying failures destabilises (2411.02337#s3).

condition_checks.reason: No expert exact-action mismatch reward.
condition_checks.condition_definition: Valid alternative actions are treated as mismatches and non-expert branches never see real next states (2509.11543#s1, 2509.11543#s3).

condition_checks.reason: Long-horizon cases and3 difficulty levels, but no benchmark run-to-run spread.
condition_checks.condition_definition: Evaluated on short tasks only, with few repeats and on subsets (WebArena-Lite) (2406.11896#s1, 2411.02337#s3).

condition_checks.reason: 4B/8B final models, detailed STR ablation8B only.
condition_checks.condition_name: Gains not shown across model sizes
condition_checks.condition_definition: Gains shrink with model size (2509.11543#s1).

condition_checks.reason: Task checker calibration exists; per-step memory correctness unvalidated.
condition_checks.condition_name: Unvalidated error labels and environment assumptions
condition_checks.condition_definition: MLLM verifier/first-error labels are not validated against humans, the method assumes Back restores the previous screen, and covers visual/grounding but not high-level planning errors; reflection tuning is not isolated by ablation (2506.08012#s1, 2506.08012#s2, 2501.12326#s1).

condition_checks.reason: Teacher reasoning noise not independently measured.
condition_checks.condition_definition: Single-sample system-2 decoding is worse in-domain (irrelevant/hallucinated reasoning); redundant actions in source trajectories yield wrong reasoning (7.8%); an observation-description (L3) level misleads at inference and self-correction is conjectured rather than isolated (2501.12326#s2, 2412.04454#s2, 2508.09123#s3, 2508.09123#s2).

claims.text: ATMem-UI-8B reaches 76.6% on AndroidWorld, beating UI-TARS-2-230B (73.3) and 8B peers (MAI-UI 70.7, GUI-Owl-1.5-Thinking 71.6).
claims.setting: Qwen3-VL-8B + SFT on 21.7K steps + STR-GRPO; AndroidWorld 116 tasks
claims.baseline_control: Published numbers for other agents; own ablation chain Baseline 47.6 -> SFT 70.7 -> GRPO 74.8 -> STR-GRPO 76.6
claims.selection_vs_test: 20-app virtual training platform built in AndroidWorld style; overlap not analysed
claims.result_denominator: run count unstated; rates not multiples of 1/116
claims.counterevidence: MAI-UI-235B scores 76.7 in a pinned source and is not in the table; ATMem-free SFT arm absent.
claims.allowed_conclusion: In the authors setting the full pipeline outperforms listed 8B and 230B baselines on AndroidWorld; the memory structure contribution itself is not isolated.

claims.text: Structured memory generalises to unseen MobileWorld environments (23.3 vs 16.1 for GELab-Zero 4B).
claims.selection_vs_test: author statement that environments are unseen
claims.counterevidence: No app-overlap analysis; MobileWorld contains different task types (author text) which could favour the training.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Consistent ordering vs listed baselines on a second online benchmark; unseen-ness not verified by us.

claims.text: STR-GRPO yields selective memory use and higher SR than GRPO.
claims.counterevidence: Alpha and learning rate unstated; one run
claims.allowed_conclusion: Directional: Mem% down 14 points with SR up 1.8-2.6 points.

claims.text: DataScope exposes stuck loops and ATMem-UI is best among end-to-end agents at every level.
claims.counterevidence: GPT-5.2+UIIns is far higher on V1/V2 progress and scope.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Directional only; success counts too small for ranking.

claims.text: ATMem-UI-8B is the strongest on MobileWorld (+7.2 over the strongest non-ours baseline; 36.2% relative over the strongest baseline).
claims.baseline/control: Table 2 rows copied from published reports
claims.result/denominator: 23.3 vs listed 16.1/17.1; omitted MAI-UI-8B 27.5 and Doubao-1.5-UI-TARS 26.3
claims.counterevidence: agg:T-A03, agg:T-A04, agg:T-A05: same-column published values above 23.3 for baselines the paper itself uses elsewhere.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Online success (executable checkers) on MobileWorld, whose apps (Mall4Uni, Mattermost, Mastodon, ...) are not the AndroidWorld-style training apps and are declared unseen; this meets EVIDENCE.md's unseen-environment branch for the improvement over the paper's own base/SFT controls (9.4 -> 23.3). 'Unseen' is author-asserted; no app-overlap audit. It does not imply superiority on that benchmark.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported single runs: the SFT+STR-GRPO recipe on Qwen3-VL-8B reaches 76.6 on AndroidWorld (in-domain apps) and 23.3 on declared-unseen MobileWorld, +1.8/+2.6 over SFT+GRPO while invoking memory in fewer tasks; it leads the listed end-to-end agents on the authors' DataScope at floor-level success (2/32, 2/32, 1/32).
contradicted_subclaims: 'Strongest baseline'/'36.2% relative improvement' on MobileWorld: the pinned MAI-UI report, in the same GUI-only column ATMem copies its other rows from, lists MAI-UI-8B 27.5 and Doubao-1.5-UI-TARS 26.3 (both baselines elsewhere in this paper) above 23.3.
not_supported: That the structured memory itself, rather than environment-matched SFT/RL data, causes the gains (no ATMem-free SFT arm)
Inference-cost savings (task-level Mem% is not a cost)
assessment.retention_trace: Training-time: SFT policy -> balanced ON/OFF rollouts -> verifier reward minus memory-activity cost, group-normalised -> policy weights -> AndroidWorld/MobileWorld/DataScope. Memory itself is per-episode, not retained across tasks.

G.reason: Both seats: concrete item-status/eligibility/completion bottleneck with failure evidence (stuck loops 40.9%) and an experience-vs-execution memory lineage; universal 'passive memory' framing too broad for 4.

M.reason: Both seats: explicit state interface plus balanced-channel RL objective give testable predictions; OFF condition is out-of-distribution for the imitation policy and status labels are self-assigned.

X.reason: Both seats 3. With Boxes A.3/A.7 read, prompts are present (son55's 'absent' deduction not applied); remaining gaps: prose schema (Workflow/Constraints/locked) differs from the prompt schema, alpha and learning rate unstated, evaluation step cap not given.

E.measurement.reason: Both seats: executable AndroidWorld/MobileWorld checkers and calibrated DataScope verifiers; no legal-alternative audit, non-integer AndroidWorld rate, floor-level DataScope success.

E.causality.reason: Both seats: SFT/GRPO/STR chain and ON/OFF intervention support the RL part; no ATMem-free SFT arm or trained flat-memory arm; teacher is a stronger proprietary planner.

E.holdout.reason: AndroidWorld and DataScope are in-domain (20-app AndroidWorld-style training platform; DataScope on AndroidWorld apps; no overlap analysis), leaving MobileWorld as the only declared-unseen test. There the improvement over the paper's own base/SFT is genuine held-out evidence, but the paper's comparative transfer claim ('strongest baseline', +36.2%) is contradicted by same-column published values for baselines the paper itself uses (MAI-UI-8B 27.5, Doubao-1.5-UI-TARS 26.3). Claim scope exceeds and is partly refuted by the held-out evidence: between anchors 0 and 2.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats: no runs/intervals; 76.6 not k/116; DataScope differences of one task in 32.

E.cost.reason: Actual training compute is disclosed (128 H20 GPUs, ~2 h SFT, ~3 days RL, 200 containers) and memory invocation is reported per task, which is relevant cost evidence; inference tokens/latency of carrying the memory, teacher (GPT-5) data cost and budget-matched baselines are missing. Anchor 2.
